title: Pressure-Volume Loops: Preload, Afterload and Contractility
subject: Physiology
preview: The left ventricular pressure-volume loop displays filling, isovolumetric contraction, ejection and isovolumetric relaxation.
quickRevision: The left ventricular pressure-volume loop displays filling, isovolumetric contraction, ejection and isovolumetric relaxation.
Increasing afterload tends to reduce stroke volume for a given contractility and preload.
Greater contractility increases the slope of end-systolic pressure-volume relation and lowers end-systolic volume.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: The left ventricular pressure-volume loop displays filling, isovolumetric contraction, ejection and isovolumetric relaxation.
Increasing preload generally increases end-diastolic volume and stroke volume within physiological limits.

sections.title: Clinical application
points: Increasing afterload tends to reduce stroke volume for a given contractility and preload.
Greater contractility increases the slope of end-systolic pressure-volume relation and lowers end-systolic volume.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Changes are interdependent; an altered loop should be interpreted using the axis, valve events and clinical setting.
